launches.title: Almanac: The agent with a company brain
launches.tagline: Almanac works with its own browser and terminal, signed into the accounts you connect.
launches.body:
There's a new kind of agent.

It exists on its own computer, connected to your tools, with a living brain of everything you and your company know.

Introducing Almanac, the agent with a company brain.

<https://youtu.be/UZVOJTQhW1I?is=Bb0d2--YkZYf7xdp>

Almanac works with its own browser and terminal, signed into the accounts you connect. Everything in your tools compiles into a wiki that it reads before every task. Your teammates' Almanacs share that wiki. You text it work. It texts you when it's done.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106258&key=user_uploads/2550783/615174e2-3d24-480d-a8f5-7c849c5a24b9)

**What we hand ours**

* Divit has it gather feedback from our customer Slack channels and file GitHub issues, with screenshots and reproduction steps.
* Kushagra connected his Chase account. It inspects recurring charges and cancels subscriptions he doesn't use.
* Before meetings, it sends us a brief built from our past emails and calendar. After, it drafts the follow-up. The draft is usually good enough to send.
* It watches our production environment. When something trivial breaks, it fixes it and raises a PR.
* It buys our dinner. At this point it suggests the order.

**It knows when to stop.** At a login, a payment, or a decision it shouldn't make alone, it pings you or hands you the live browser.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106258&key=user_uploads/2550783/9b85821d-c37b-4da7-87a9-6218d731ad53)

**Automations are just sentences.** "Whenever a customer reports a bug, check whether anyone else has reported it, reproduce it, and update the GitHub issue." Say it once. There's no workflow builder.

**The brain is shared.** Your teammates' Almanacs read and write the same wiki. So can your other agents: Claude Code and Codex can start caught up on your company. \
\
**Our bet.** We're Rohan, Kushagra, and Divit. We grew up together in India and met 11 years ago preparing for the JEE. Since then: machine-learning research and engineering across Vector Institute, CMU, MIT, Harvard, and Arcesium. From the start we've had one bet: AI will need a context layer, and it takes the shape of a wiki. For the last year and a half we've built agent wikis for Harvard, for NASA, and once, an attempt at the whole internet. We are, perhaps predictably, obsessed with wikis. Almanac is that bet, pointed at your company.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106258&key=user_uploads/2550783/7bab1366-3e4c-4140-829d-e1bc9666d9ab)

Text it your first task tonight. See what's done by morning.\
\
Try it out today: <https://usealmanac.com>

launches.title: Touchy 🙌: Voice-first AI Assistant for iPhone that understands the world around you
launches.tagline: Your personal AI assistant that sees what you see, remembers what matters to you, and gets things done across all your tools. Just ask out loud.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We’re building Touchy 🙌, a voice and image-first AI assistant for the iPhone that personalizes itself to you. You can activate Touchy from your lock screen to instantly get things done across your apps or get answers about the world around you. Touchy is free to try, get it here: <https://apps.apple.com/us/app/touchy-ai-at-your-fingertips/id6798889392>

<https://youtube.com/shorts/IJNucvAZ_-k>

## **The Problem**

You probably know the feeling:

You ask the assistant on your phone, across the room, to send a colleague a message.

It cheerfully replies that it found 10 search results for “text Bob on Slack”.

So you trudge to your phone, find the app, open the DM, and begrudgingly type out your message instead.

We wanted a better personal assistant, one that had the intelligence and integrations we’ve come to expect from our AI agents, with the convenience of one that was native to your devices. We also believe that for AI to truly be personal, it needs to be deeply integrated into your life and the world around you. Right now, AI systems are constrained largely to using digital tools, yet the physical world is rich with audio and visual information that your phone is capable of receiving.

## What We Built

So we built Touchy. One button press and you're instantly talking to an assistant that can see what you see, remember what you've said, and take action across all the tools you use. 

What sets Touchy apart:

* **Reimagined UX.** Touchy is a fast, fully iOS-native app with a unique interface that is delightful to use and brings it closer to the world around you.
* **Sees and hears the world around you**. Speak to Touchy and it can speak back. Easily snap a photo with the app’s camera to give Touchy access to what you’re seeing.
* **Gets things done across your apps**. Touchy comes with built-in integrations with 1,000+ popular apps, as well as iOS-native capabilities such as you contacts and location.
* **Make it yours over time**. You chat with Touchy in a single, continuous conversation. It automatically collects memories and preferences, and tailors itself to be more useful to you as you use it.

It's built to give you your attention back. Ask it something, let it act, and get back to your day — no app fighting for your attention.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111407&key=user_uploads/3697324/23ce7916-fce5-44c4-9ebf-f04049fee639)

## The team

We’re Rohit, Andrew, and Kev. Before this, Rohit was doing a PhD on AI alignment at Google DeepMind Princeton and graduated #1 in Berkeley EECS. Andrew built educational software that scaled to half a million students worldwide. Kev was a startup founding engineer, developing data and GPU infrastructure that power many of the leading AI neolabs today. 

We met during undergrad at UC Berkeley, and we’re coming back together to research, productionize, and scale the future of personal technology.

## Our ask

If you have an iPhone, download Touchy and try it out: <https://apps.apple.com/us/app/touchy-ai-at-your-fingertips/id6798889392>

We would love to learn what people find themselves using Touchy for, and what they wish they could use it for. You can also report bugs by shaking your phone or just telling Touchy. You can also reach us at [founders@touchyapp.com](mailto:founders@touchyapp.com)

name: herdr
long_description:
Developers don't run one coding agent anymore. They run fleets of them — for hours, sometimes days — across laptops, servers, and sandboxes. Keeping track of that work is the new bottleneck: which agent is blocked, which one finished, which terminal is it in, and why did everything die when the laptop closed.

Herdr is the open-source home for that work. A background server owns the agents' terminal sessions on each machine, so the work survives disconnects, closed lids, and dropped SSH. Herdr detects each agent and turns the chaos into an attention queue — working, blocked, done, across every project — so you look only when an agent needs you. Every client is just a view: the bundled terminal UI, SSH from another machine, your phone. Close one, open another; the work never stops.

Software can drive it too: a CLI, a socket API, and a plugin marketplace that passed 500 community plugins in its first month. The runtime is Apache-2.0 and stays open. Four months after launch: 25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads.
